**Highway to the Danger Zone.** Squachy got his license. Specifically, he got a Marauder V8: justcallmekoko's ESP32-C5 board, with a GPS, a battery gauge and an SD slot, which is a polite way of saying "a surveillance detector that wants to go for a drive." So now it can. Turn on WARDRIVE, take it outside, and every WiFi network and Bluetooth gadget it hears goes into a WiGLE file on the SD card, pinned to where you were when you heard it. Squachy rides shotgun. He does not have a license. Please do not tell anyone.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.36.0/docs/highway-to-the-danger-zone.gif" width="480" alt="On a 2.8 inch screen, Squachy stands in front of a synthwave sunset with a small GPS badge lit at the top and a lava lamp battery gauge in the top left corner. The DIAGNOSTICS page lists GPS satellites, a fix, and a WARDRIVE line reading ON, 42 written, with the WiGLE file's name below. Then a small grey yeti dances the disco next to Squachy in a night forest, then flosses. Last, the yeti is thrown, lands face down at Squachy's feet saying OOF, Squachy yells Hey! Watch the feet., and the yeti gets up and stomps off saying NOT TOY."></p>

**The Marauder V8 (BETA).** It's on the flasher. Marauder keeps the V8's screen wiring a secret (it's built in a private step), so we did what any reasonable cryptid would do: we asked every pin. A little test program tried every possible arrangement of wires until the screen answered "I'm an ILI9341" and the touch chip told us its temperature. Then we lit one pin at a time until the backlight came on. Turns out it's wired exactly like the NM-CYD-C5, which made everything else easy. It has a real battery gauge (actual percent, and it knows when it's charging), its little activity light breathes like the status lights on the other boards, it scans 5 GHz too, and its battery lamp is now twice the size. Thanks, **justcallmekoko**, for the board.

**And the T-Deck Plus (BETA).** Two new boards in one release, because a LilyGo T-Deck Plus landed on the bench the same afternoon and it was too good to leave: an ESP32-S3 handheld with a 2.8" screen, capacitive touch, a GPS, an SD slot, a speaker, a 2000 mAh battery, and a REAL KEYBOARD. Type a squad message on actual keys. Type the WiFi password without poking at glass. Enter sends, backspace backspaces, and alt+B lights the keys up in the dark. It wardrives like the V8. Its backlight turned out to be a chip that counts pulses instead of taking a brightness, which is the sort of thing you only find out by making the screen flicker like a disco, so now we count pulses. The trackball and the LoRa radio sit this one out. The radio shares its wiring with the screen, and the two have not yet learned to take turns without the picture paying for it. They're in couples counselling. They come later.

**Wardriving.** **jotra7** built GPS and wardriving for the CYD (PR #46), and the V8 drives with it. WARDRIVE is in Settings and tells you what's up: NO CARD, WAITING FOR FIX, or how many rows it's written. The GPS also sets the clock with no WiFi, puts a position on every catch in the SD log, and shows its fix on the main screen and in DIAGNOSTICS. Speaking of the SD log: it used to name every file "day zero," forever, on every board. Now it's one file per date, with the real time on every row.

**Faster on the C5.** The ESP32-C5 has no math co-processor, so every time SYNTHWAVE did a little trigonometry for the water (up to six times per row, a hundred-something rows) the chip did it longhand, like a kid in detention. It took 70 ms a frame. Now it uses a lookup table and takes 4.6. SYNTHWAVE went from 8 to 20 frames a second, THE GIBSON from 11 to 17, and it looks exactly the same. The NM-CYD-C5 gets all of it too.

**The yeti has moves.** Tap him and he dances: SATURDAY NIGHT YETI (full disco floor) or THE FLOSS (sweaty finish, very proud). When Squachy dances, the yeti joins in. Pick him up and throw him and he flies like the other pets, lands face-first with an "OOF.", and stomps off muttering "NOT TOY." Until you discover each trick, he drops hints. Loudly. In yeti.

**POWER OFF, properly this time.** Sometimes waking the Freenove boards from POWER OFF showed you a second of picture and then died, and BOOT couldn't bring it back, because it wasn't asleep, it was stuck. It got stuck starting WiFi, but only when nothing on the other end of the USB cable was listening (a charger, say), which is why it never once did it while we were watching. Now a wake restarts itself once, in half a second, the clean way, and it has woken 24 times out of 24. And if anything ever hangs on a wake again, it restarts in seconds instead of sitting there dead.

**Squad messages that actually arrive.** In a busy room the boards switch to quiet listening, and quiet listening could not hear squad messages at all, which was most rooms, including ours. **retrodroid32** fixed it (PR #48): we tested it on two boards, 0 messages out of 8 got through before, 8 out of 8 after, in under a second. retrodroid32 also made the raw scan rows say WATCH, HUNT and IGNORE right there in the list (PR #44).

**And.** **T0x0pl4sm4** added the Freenove ESP32-S3 4.0" (PR #51). It builds from source for now, and goes on the flasher once a few more people have run it. An NVIDIA Shield is no longer a gunshot detector (#41). The C5's WiFi password keyboard stopped strobing between capitals and lower case (#52). CALIBRATE TOUCH no longer turns the screen white on the C5 and Freenove boards. The host's speech bubble stays in front of a visitor, the intro screen's bubble got out of the way, and the 3.5" visit's message button moved out from under the visitor's words. The black box finally works on the two C5 boards: its spot in flash turned out to be inside the app, so it had been quietly switched off the whole time. We found that out by drawing a picture of the flash. Pictures are important.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- The Marauder V8 (justcallmekoko, ESP32-C5) as a BETA on the flasher: ILI9341 at 40 MHz, resistive touch, SD, MAX17048 battery gauge, GPS, activity LED, 5 GHz scanning.
- The LilyGo T-Deck Plus (ESP32-S3) as a BETA on the flasher: ST7789 at 40 MHz, GT911 touch, the keyboard typing into the message, name, PIN and WiFi password screens, speaker, SD, battery, GPS wardriving. Trackball and LoRa not yet.
- GPS and wardriving on the CYD GPS builds, the V8 and the T-Deck (from PR #46 by jotra7): WARDRIVE in Settings writes a WiGLE file to the SD card; the fix sets the clock, goes on SD log rows and the alert card, and shows on the main screen and in DIAGNOSTICS.
- The yeti pet's dances (tap him), his throw, his hints, and dancing along with Squachy.
- The Freenove ESP32-S3 4.0" (FNK0104S), build from source (PR #51 by T0x0pl4sm4).
- WATCH, HUNT and IGNORE on raw scan rows (PR #44 by retrodroid32).
- Console: `POWERLOG` (the power diary), `NAPTEST`, `YETI DISCO`, `YETI FLOSS`.

**Changed**
- SD log files are named by date (`squachwatch-YYYYMMDD.log`) and rows start with the real time once the clock is set (from PR #46 by jotra7).
- SYNTHWAVE and THE GIBSON draw with whole-number maths: 2.5x and 1.5x faster on the ESP32-C5.
- The battery lamp is twice the size against the left edge on 320-wide screens.
- Squad messages and invites travel in the main advert, so boards on passive scanning receive them, with transmit retries and MESH TX / RX lines in DIAGNOSTICS (PR #48 by retrodroid32).
- Raven matches only its five known service numbers.

**Fixed**
- Waking the Freenove S3 boards from POWER OFF could hang starting WiFi when no computer was reading the USB port.
- A guessed clock was treated as real after a restart.
- The C5's WiFi keyboard flickered between capitals and lower case (#52).
- An NVIDIA Shield showed up as a Raven (#41).
- CALIBRATE TOUCH could leave the screen white on the C5 and Freenove S3 boards.
- The black box was switched off on the NM-CYD-C5 and Marauder V8.
- The host's speech bubble went behind a visitor; the intro bubble covered the scene; the 3.5" message button sat under the visitor's bubble.
